title: Provisional measurement review
notice: These are newly derived, unvalidated educational observations. The source supplies no printed answer key for this exercise. They are unscored and require qualified ECG educator review.

fields.basis: Visually checked ventricular peaks and measured R–R intervals in original PDF 506
fields.reason: R–R intervals: 1.228 s, 1.203 s, 1.228 s, 1.22 s. These describe the short displayed sample, not an independently adjudicated rhythm diagnosis.

fields.value: Atrial identity unresolved: Tiny pre-QRS excursions are approximately 2–3 original pixels high and comparable to line/baseline variation. Repetition supports a candidate but does not establish P onset.
fields.basis: Original PDF page 506; repeated-complex visual review and independent source comparison
fields.reason: Provisional visible-deflection description, not validated atrial identity, atrial origin, or a diagnosis. Qualified ECG educator review is outstanding.

fields.basis: Original PDF page 506; independently reconciled endpoint bands and horizontal grid; assumes course 25 mm/s (0.04 s per small square), not a verified per-strip speed
fields.reason: Distinct rapid ventricular deflections return to a nearly flat local baseline; duration remains a pixel-limited range. Approximate reader-union envelope, conditional on course speed. This envelope includes reader and endpoint uncertainty; it is not a confidence interval, normal/abnormal classification, or proof of beat-to-beat physiological variation.

fields.value: Regular slow rhythm around 49 bpm; small pre-QRS deflections appear present, but origin deferred.
fields.basis: New provisional educational interpretation, not an original publisher key
fields.reason: Not reviewed by a qualified ECG educator. Do not use this as a scored answer or patient diagnosis.

limitations: New wave-field estimates remain provisional and unscored. Range width reflects uncertain endpoints and reader disagreement, not a validated diagnostic category. QT/QTc, calibrated amplitudes and clinical diagnosis are not established.
The exact original PDF was checked. The inspected waveforms are embedded rasters; larger rendering does not add samples. Expert interpretation may still improve unresolved component identification.

P-wave identity unresolved: Tiny pre-QRS excursions are approximately 2–3 original pixels high and comparable to line/baseline variation. Repetition supports a candidate but does not establish P onset.
PR interval unresolved: No numeric PR estimate: P identity or its distinct onset remains unresolved. Candidate x bands are search targets only, not measurable P onsets.
Calibration assumes the course’s 25 mm/s convention (PDF pages 228, 230, 231 and 234). Every image grid was checked separately; the assumption is not a per-strip speed label.
Peak positions are approximate to about ±2 source pixels; morphology, low-amplitude P waves and boundaries remain uncertain. This is not a statistical confidence interval.
